svg.title: The spotter verification ladder
svg.desc: How a trained vision model becomes a claim anyone can check. The trained PyTorch model is exported to a weights JSON, and batch normalization is folded into the convolution weights on the way out, so the deployed network is plain convolutions with no normalization layers. That JSON then goes down two independent paths. The float path runs a numpy forward pass and must reproduce the stored logits to within a tolerance of 1e-4 and match the stored per-pixel argmax exactly. The int8 path first quantizes: weights per output channel, symmetric, scaled by the channel maximum over 127, and activations per tensor, symmetric, scaled by a percentile of the absolute activation measured on seeded calibration frames rather than by the maximum. Its integer forward pass must then reproduce the stored argmax bit for bit, agree with the float path on at least 99 percent of pixels, and hold per-class intersection over union at 0.98 or better against the float masks. Only when both gates pass does the golden bundle in the deploy directory exist. The bundle is the seam: everything above it is how the numbers were produced, and everything below it is anyone proving they reproduced them. A hardware port in C, on an FPGA, or on a phone swaps in its own forward implementation and runs the same verify script unchanged.
svg.text: Both gates must pass before the bundle exists.
Any port reruns verify.py unchanged: C, FPGA, phone.
